candidate_relations.reason: Basal cell carcinoma is a related keratinocytic cancer but conflicts with squamous histology.
Bowler/interdigital ulcer describes the chronic macerated ulcer, a manifestation rather than the squamous carcinoma.
Chronic ulcer names the enlarging fissured lesion, not the requested squamous cell carcinoma.
Eczema is a different inflammatory dermatosis from invasive squamous cell carcinoma.
Chronic lymphedema is a different condition and is not described as the final diagnosis.
Mycetoma is a deep fungal/actinomycotic infection, not squamous cell carcinoma.
Chronic ulcerative keratosis is not the same diagnostic object as squamous cell carcinoma.
Chronic interdigital ulcer is the clinical wound, not the squamous malignancy.
Chronic interdigital foot ulcer restates the ulcerated site rather than squamous cell carcinoma.
Squamous cell carcinoma of the foot is the same carcinoma with compatible anatomy of the fourth interdigital ulcer.
Fungal foot infection was already treated without improvement and is not the reference carcinoma.
Squamous cell carcinoma matches the full reference diagnostic object.
Keratosis is a different, typically non-invasive keratinocytic lesion from squamous cell carcinoma.
Keratoacanthoma is a related keratinocytic neoplasm with conflicting clinicopathologic identity versus SCC.
Malignant melanoma is a related cutaneous malignancy but conflicts on melanocytic versus squamous lineage.
Chronic pyoderma gangrenosum is a neutrophilic ulcerating disease, not squamous cell carcinoma.
Pyoderma gangrenosum is a different ulcerative dermatosis from SCC.
Bacterial infection may secondarily colonize the ulcer but is not the squamous carcinoma.
Hyperkeratotic ulcer describes the verrucous wound morphology rather than the carcinoma.
Deep mycosis is a different infectious diagnosis from squamous cell carcinoma.
